J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "For an element h in H, hgP = gP is equivalent to P = ghg^(-1)P." First-choice line 27 reads "Then for every *h* in *H*, we have hgP = gP, which is equivalent to P = ghg^(-1)P, which is equivalent to ghg^(-1) being an element of P." That is verbatim the challenged equivalence (its first link). Active assumptions: line 13 (|G| = p^r m with p not dividing m, P a Sylow p-subgroup), line 15 (H a p-subgroup), line 23 (H acts by left multiplication on the left cosets G/P) and line 25 (gP is a fixed point of that action).

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A completely instantiated witness: "In S_3, if P is the subgroup generated by (1 2), g = (1 2 3), and h = (2 3), then hgP = gP holds but ghg^{-1} = (1 3) is not in P, so P != ghg^{-1}P." The group, the Sylow subgroup, the coset representative, the element h and the value of the conjugate are all given explicitly.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact enumeration of the supplied witness in S_3, script kept, using the usual composition (ab)(x) = a(b(x)). Every active assumption is met: |S_3| = 6 = 2^1 * 3 with p = 2 not dividing 3; P = {e,(1 2)} has order 2 and so is a Sylow 2-subgroup; H = {e,(2 3)} is a 2-subgroup; and gP = {(1 2 3),(1 3)} is genuinely a fixed point of the H-action on left cosets (the script checks kgP = gP for every k in H). On this witness hgP = gP holds, while g h g^{-1} = (1 3) is not in P and therefore ghg^{-1}P = {(1 3),(1 2 3)} is not P. So the left-hand side of line 27's equivalence holds and the right-hand side fails: the equivalence as written is refuted at a point satisfying all of the source's assumptions. The script also confirms the reversed conjugate g^{-1} h g = (1 2) does lie in P, which pins the defect as the direction of conjugation in line 27 rather than anything else.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The saved response is only the JSON object: one candidate label, the challenged claim and the counterexample. It draws no further consequence -- it does not assert that the second Sylow theorem or the conclusion at line 29 is false -- so there is no stated consequence that could overreach.

notes: Convention dependency a second reader should weigh, which I checked explicitly in the script: the witness works under the usual right-to-left composition (ab)(x) = a(b(x)), the convention that matches the source's 'left multiplication on the left cosets' at line 23. Under the opposite left-to-right convention the premise hgP = gP already fails for this g and h, and the witness would not apply. I did not adjust the witness for that case. Substantively the located defect is one of direction only: line 27 should conjugate by g^{-1} (g^{-1}hg in P), and the theorem statement at line 17 is untouched by this because g there ranges over all of G.
